_about: Demo K (consent vs confidentiality). Single source for the static HTML in m07.html (written by scripts/invisible_engine/content/inserts.py) and for consent.js; tested by invisible-engine/tests/demos.mjs. The point: encryption decides who ELSE can read a location; it never decides whether the person being located agreed.

levels.label: No encryption
levels.note: A teaching extreme: reports travel and are stored readable.

levels.label: Encrypted in transit only
levels.note: Protected on the wire (TLS), readable by the service that stores it.

levels.label: End-to-end encrypted
levels.note: Only the owner’s devices hold the key that opens a report (the design Apple, Google and Samsung document).

levels.label: End-to-end, post-quantum ready
levels.note: The same, with key exchange designed to resist a future quantum computer (Modules 8–10).

scenarios.label: A lost bag
scenarios.story: The account holder put the tag in their own bag and lost it at a station. The location shown is the bag’s.
scenarios.consent: Nobody else is being located. Strong encryption protects the owner from the relay and from anyone on the network.

scenarios.label: A tag hidden in someone’s bag
scenarios.story: Someone put a tag they control into another person’s bag. The location shown is that person’s.
scenarios.consent: Strong encryption keeps the relay and the network out, and in doing so keeps the misuse private too. The account holder sees the same locations at every setting. Encryption cannot tell a lost bag from a person being followed.

helps: An alert on the carrier’s own phone when an unknown tracker, separated from its owner, seems to travel with them (iPhone and Android, through a shared specification).
A sound from a separated tag when it is moved.
A tap with any NFC phone, which shows the tag’s serial number and part of the owner’s details for a tag found moving with you.
Platform safety tools such as Apple’s Safety Check and its Personal Safety User Guide, and Google’s acceptable use policy for Find Hub.
People: someone you trust, local support services, and the police where appropriate.
helps_note: None of these depend on the encryption setting. They protect consent, which encryption does not.
safety: If you think a tracker is being used to follow you, consider your safety first: disabling it can alert the person who placed it. Apple’s and Google’s safety guides describe the options.
